Cc: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@oakridgelabs.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot credits and procurement timeline

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team is excited about Redwood’s latency profile and the quantization guidance you shared. Quick situation update from our side: procurement is taking longer than expected because Oakridge is on a new vendor onboarding track for Q3.

We exhausted the standard PLG sandbox allotment (we pushed a heavier integration test than anticipated) and are now blocked from completing the final integration run. Without one small top-up of credits and an extra 30 days on the pilot window, we won’t be able to finalize the security sign-off before the next board review (which delays a purchase decision and a large POC).

Could Redwood provide a one-off safety-net grant of 75k token-equivalent credits and extend the sandbox by 30 days? We will send the PO and procurement contact details this afternoon (attached is a stub PO showing expected timelines). We understand these are non-standard asks and are happy to accept a short-term usage cap and reporting requirement if that helps.

Appreciate any flexibility you can provide — we’d like to keep momentum and get to a paid deployment by September.

Best,
Susan Park
Head of ML Ops, Oakridge Labs

Tessa / Marissa —

Brief context from deal desk: Oakridge fits our strategic target for bioinformatics (strong case study potential, likely to convert to Dedicated in 6–9 months). We do sometimes grant limited top-ups for procurement friction, but this request (75k tokens + 30 days) sits above the standard manual top-ups our AE team can approve.

If we’re comfortable with a conditional grant, here’s what I recommend before asking Jonas to approve formally:
- Require PO receipt (can be a stub) and procurement contact on file.
- Cap the one-off free usage to the 75k token estimate with an emergency kill-switch if usage deviates >25%.
- Add a short-term SLA: weekly usage summary to the AE and a single check-in at the end of the extension.
- Convert to a purchase order by the end of the extension or credits stop.

Assuming we accept those terms, I’ll ask Jonas for a one-time exec override. Tessa — please confirm customer PO ETA and whether they’ll accept the reporting.

Thanks for the concise summary, team. I’m comfortable approving a one-time safety-net concession with the following conditions:

1) Grant 75,000 token-equivalent free credits to Oakridge Labs and extend their sandbox by 30 days starting the day we apply the credits.
2) Credits are capped; any usage beyond the 75k estimate triggers an automatic pause and a mandatory AE review.
3) Customer must provide the PO (even a stub) within 72 hours of credit application and confirm procurement contact. If PO is not received in that window, credits are revoked.
4) AE (Tessa) to submit a short weekly usage summary into the HubSpot deal (deal id DL-2026-0417) for the duration of the extension.
5) This is a one-off exec override tied to this account and does not change published PLG policy.

Tessa — please apply the credits when you have the PO. Aditya, please record the exception in the deal desk log and notify Revenue Ops so finance can track the concession.
